sentences.en: Lisa, you wanted to respond to something Nate said right before the break.
sentences.zh: 丽莎，你刚才想回应内特在休息前说的一些话。

sentences.en: Nate, correct me if I'm wrong.
sentences.zh: 内特，如果我记错了，请纠正我。

sentences.en: It seemed to be that in the Northeast and the upper Midwest, some of the Democratic candidates' leads and even their victories were not as big as a place like the Sunbelt.
sentences.zh: 似乎在东北部和中西部上游，一些民主党候选人的领先优势甚至胜利，都没有像阳光地带那样大。

sentences.en: And I wonder if it's because the candidates running in the Northeast, the upper Midwest, the Democrats tended to be more progressive.
sentences.zh: 我想知道，这是否是因为在东北部和中西部上游参选的民主党人往往更加进取。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think Nate was talking about the difference between how candidates fared in the Sunbelt and sort of these northern states, Minnesota, Michigan, and Maine.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为内特刚才谈到了候选人在阳光地带和这些北方州（如明尼苏达州、密歇根州和缅因州）表现的差异。

sentences.en: And I think it is worth pointing out that those are states where Democrats ran self-proclaimed progressives, candidates who saw themselves on the more left flank of the party.
sentences.zh: 我认为值得指出的是，在这些州，民主党人推出的都是自称的进派人士，他们认为自己属于党内更偏左的一翼。

sentences.en: And the candidates who ran in places like Kansas and Texas and Iowa saw themselves as postpartisan, that they tried to put distance between themselves and the Democratic national
sentences.zh: 而在堪萨斯州、得克萨斯州和艾奥瓦州等地参选的候选人则把自己视为超越党派的人，他们试图与民主党全国

sentences.en: brand.
sentences.zh: 品牌保持距离。

sentences.en: They cast themselves as centrists, as people who want to work across the aisle.
sentences.zh: 他们把自己塑造为温和派，是那些希望跨越党派合作的人。

sentences.en: So you have two different brands of Democrat, really, who won tonight.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，今晚获胜的是两种不同品牌的民主党人。

sentences.en: And I think a part of what you're seeing is a big Democratic tent, which is, of course, what Democrats have wanted and talked about wanting since they loSt.
sentences.zh: 我认为你所看到的一部分是一个包容的大帐篷式的民主党，这当然也是民主党人在落败后一直想要并谈论想要的。

sentences.en: Not let miss tests.
sentences.zh: 不要让测试漏掉。

sentences.en: Letting lots of different kinds of Democrats run for the places where they're running.
sentences.zh: 让各种各样的民主党人去他们能够参选的地方参选。

sentences.en: But sometimes big tents can cause big intra-party fights underneath them.
sentences.zh: 但有时大帐篷也会在其内部引发激烈的党内斗争。

sentences.en: So I think we'll see a continuation of this debate that Democrats have been having at this point for many years over what the direction of their party should be.
sentences.zh: 因此，我认为我们将会看到这场辩论的延续，民主党人就党的发展方向已经进行了多年的辩论。

sentences.en: In a midterm, it's enough to just run against an unpopular president.
sentences.zh: 在中期选举中，仅仅靠反对一个不受欢迎的总统就足够了。

sentences.en: Presidential campaigns are contests about the future of the country.
sentences.zh: 总统竞选是关于国家未来的较量。

sentences.en: And Democrats will need a vision, a shared vision, to put forward in those races.
sentences.zh: 民主党人需要在这些竞选中提出一个愿景，一个共同的愿景。

sentences.en: And we'll see them fight it out over what that should be over the next year.
sentences.zh: 我们将在接下来的一年里看到他们为这个愿景争论不休。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Big Democratic victory, you're saying, basically doesn't necessarily resolve any of the big internal questions and battles inside the party.
sentences.zh: 你是说，民主党的大胜基本上不一定能解决党内的任何重大内部问题和争端。

sentences.en: I think that there is a North and South realignment happening.
sentences.zh: 我认为南北方的重组正在发生。

sentences.en: And you can really see it tonight.
sentences.zh: 你今晚确实能看出来这一点。

sentences.en: That the Democratic Party's ceiling is lower in the old industrial Midwest, in Ohio, where
sentences.zh: 民主党在老工业中西部（如俄亥俄州）的上限变低了，在那里，

sentences.en: Sherrod Brown had been a popular Democrat forever and is retaking a seat in the Senate, is not performing as strongly as some of these Democratic candidates in the South.
sentences.zh: 谢罗德·布朗曾长期是一位受欢迎的民主党人，现在他正在重新夺回参议院的一个席位，但他的表现却没有南方的一些民主党候选人那么强劲。

sentences.en: So there seems to be a higher ceiling where John Ossoff is in Georgia than where the Democrats seem to be able to reach in that upper Midwest area.
sentences.zh: 因此，乔恩·奥索夫所在的佐治亚州的上限似乎比民主党在中西部上中游地区所能触及的上限要高。

sentences.en: And I think that tells you a little bit where the party's future could be.
sentences.zh: 我认为这在一定程度上预示着该党未来可能的走向。

sentences.en: So I wonder if the results that we're talking about here would in any way tip the scales
sentences.zh: 所以我想知道，我们在这里讨论的结果是否会以某种方式打破平衡

sentences.en: when it comes to this debate about progressives,
sentences.zh: 在关于进派人士的这场辩论中，

sentences.en: Democratic Socialists, in favor of the centrists, or if that's just like not the right conclusion to draw given the scale of Democrats.
sentences.zh: 民主党社会主义者，倾向于温和派，或者鉴于民主党的规模，这根本不是应该得出的正确结论。

sentences.en: My text messages tonight would suggest that everybody is declaring victory, right?
sentences.zh: 我今晚的短信表明每个人都在宣布胜利，对吧？

sentences.en: The left is saying, we almost got a Democratic Socialist in Florida, right?
sentences.zh: 左翼说，我们差一点就在佛罗里达州选出了一名民主党社会主义者，对吧？

sentences.en: And the centrists are saying, look at all the actual people who won all of these hard braces.
sentences.zh: 而温和派则说，看看所有在这些艰难竞选中获胜的实际候选人。

sentences.en: So everybody's declaring victory and everybody has just enough to hang their hat on an election like this, where, again, the election was not about the Democrats.
sentences.zh: 因此，每个人都在宣布胜利，每个人都有足够的借口在这样一场选举中找到寄托，而这场选举的焦点再次不在于民主党。

sentences.en: The election was about the Republicans.
sentences.zh: 这场选举的焦点在于共和党。

sentences.en: The contrarian take here is that no one should feel good about themselves.
sentences.zh: 这里的反主流观点是，谁也不应该自我感觉良好。

sentences.en: They're just benefiting from the least popular president since 1946.
sentences.zh: 他们只是在受益于自1946年以来最不受欢迎的总统。

sentences.en: And this is still a discredited party that voters don't trust us all the names of the Democrats.
sentences.zh: 这仍然是一个声誉受损的政党，选民并不信任我们所有的民主党人。

sentences.en: And there's plenty of indicators of that in our own polling, right, where you see that Trump is unpopular,
sentences.zh: 在我们自己的民调中有很多这方面的迹象，对吧，你可以看到特朗普不受欢迎，

sentences.en: Trump is unpopular, and Democrats have improved their numbers on a lot of issues, most centrally, like who is trusted to handle the economy, which is very important always
sentences.zh: 特朗普不受欢迎，而且民主党在很多问题上的支持率有所上升，最核心的是谁更受信任来处理经济问题，这始终非常重要，

sentences.en: and particularly important in this election.
sentences.zh: 在这次选举中尤其重要。

sentences.en: But when voters are asked questions about, you know, how much they trust the Democratic Party, is it too far to the left, too far to the right, they're still pretty mixed on it.
sentences.zh: 但当选民被问及诸如他们对民主党信任程度如何、是过于偏左还是过于偏右等问题时，他们的看法仍然非常复杂。

sentences.en: Yes, voters are voting, casting their ballots for Democratic candidates.
sentences.zh: 是的，选民们正在投票，为民主党候选人投下选票。

sentences.en: Are they flocking to the National Democratic Party?
sentences.zh: 他们是否在蜂拥支持全国民主党？

sentences.en: I'm not sure we can draw that.
sentences.zh: 我不确定我们能否得出这个结论。

sentences.en: I know we can't draw that conclusion quite yet.
sentences.zh: 我知道我们现在还不能得出这个结论。

sentences.en: Well, one thing that happened tonight that, if you're a Democrat, seems like a very important and hopeful sign is that a new generation of,
sentences.zh: 好吧，今晚发生的一件对民主党人来说似乎非常重要且充满希望的事情是，新一代的

sentences.en: especially Senator Alex, a Senator James Tallarico, a Senator John Ossoff, a Senator Abdul El-Sayed, on and on, that has come up in the Trump era.
sentences.zh: 特别是亚历克斯参议员、詹姆斯·塔拉里科参议员、乔恩·奥索夫参议员、阿卜杜勒·埃尔-赛耶德参议员等等，他们在特朗普时代崛起。

sentences.en: They're so digitally native.
sentences.zh: 他们非常具有数字时代的原生特性。

sentences.en: They're so ubiquitous in the way that they campaign.
sentences.zh: 他们的竞选方式无处不在。

sentences.en: This is a future of the Democratic Party that no one was even thinking about five, six years ago.
sentences.zh: 这是民主党五六年前甚至无人想象的未来。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, now I think Democrats have a wealth of people who could run for president.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，现在我认为民主党拥有大量可以竞选总统的人才。

sentences.en: It's going to be a packed race.
sentences.zh: 这将是一场拥挤的竞选。

sentences.en: They have a very, very stocked bench of candidates.
sentences.zh: 他们有着非常、非常深厚的候选人储备。

sentences.en: And in some ways, it feels to me like the beginning of a new political era.
sentences.zh: 在某些方面，我觉得这就像是一个新政治时代的开始。

sentences.en: If you sort of look at 2006, which was another great resurgent midterm year for Democrats, ushered in this era of Obama, which remade that party.
sentences.zh: 如果你回顾2006年，那也是民主党复苏的中期选举年，它开启了奥巴马时代，重塑了那个政党。

sentences.en: The backlash to that ushered in Trump and the MAGA movement, which remade Republicans.
sentences.zh: 对其的反弹催生了特朗普和MAGA运动，重塑了共和党人。

sentences.en: And now it feels as if we're at the end of that 20-year cycle, and we're at a point where both parties are going to be looking forward to something new.
sentences.zh: 现在感觉我们正处于这20年周期的末尾，我们正处于这样一个节点：两党都将展望新的事物。

sentences.en: Democrats have these new emerging stars.
sentences.zh: 民主党拥有这些新崛起的新星。

sentences.en: Republicans have to figure out who they are at the beginnings of what could be a post-Trump moment, although we all always hesitate to say that anything is ever post-Trump.
sentences.zh: 共和党人必须在可能是后特朗普时代之初弄清楚他们是谁，尽管我们总是对任何声称是后特朗普时代的说法持保留态度。

sentences.en: It does feel now like he's a lame duck president.
sentences.zh: 现在确实感觉他成了一个跛脚鸭总统。

sentences.en: Republicans are going to have to find a way forward to keep what's left of their coalition together.
sentences.zh: 共和党人将不得不找到一条前进的道路，以维持其联盟残存的力量。

sentences.en: So I do wonder if we're sort of at the beginnings of something new for both parties and for the country's politics.
sentences.zh: 所以我确实想知道，我们是否正处于两党和国家政治新事物的开端。

sentences.en: Where does this all leave the president's party, the president's movement?
sentences.zh: 这一切把总统的政党、总统的运动置于何地？

sentences.en: What is the state of MAGA this morning?
sentences.zh: 今天早上的MAGA状态如何？

sentences.en: What is the Republican Party this morning?
sentences.zh: 今天的共和党是什么样的？

sentences.en: The Republican Party was destroyed by Donald Trump in 2016.
sentences.zh: 共和党在2016年被唐纳德·特朗普摧毁了。

sentences.en: It was reassembled around himself.
sentences.zh: 它围绕着他重新组合起来。

sentences.en: And now he's the least popular political figure heading into a midterm since 1946.
sentences.zh: 现在，他是自1946年以来迈入中期选举的最不受欢迎的政治人物。

sentences.en: And his party just suffered the worst drubbing in a half century.
sentences.zh: 他的政党刚刚遭遇了半个世纪以来最惨痛的溃败。

sentences.en: Where do we stand right now at all?
sentences.zh: 我们现在到底处境如何？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think about how much we discussed the depth of the hole that the Democratic Party found itself in after 2024.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想到了我们曾多次讨论民主党在2024年后陷入的泥潭有多深。

sentences.en: And even in that hole, everybody knew they had one big bright light, which was this coming midterm election.
sentences.zh: 即便在那个泥潭中，每个人都知道他们有一道耀眼的亮光，那就是即将到来的中期选举。

sentences.en: The Republican Party today doesn't have that bright light.
sentences.zh: 今天的共和党却没有那道亮光。

sentences.en: They have a wide open presidential primary without a clear leader.
sentences.zh: 他们面临着一个群雄逐鹿且没有明确领袖的总统初选。

sentences.en: And it's harder to rebuild at that moment than it is when you can just unite around stopping Trump.
sentences.zh: 在那种时刻重建，要比单纯团结起来阻止特朗普时困难得多。

sentences.en: Perhaps especially when the president still has a tremendous amount of clout within his party.
sentences.zh: 也许特别是当总统在党内仍然拥有巨大的影响力时。

sentences.en: In our last poll, a majority of Republicans still said they wanted to see the Republican Party continue in the Trump direction,
sentences.zh: 在我们最近的民调中，多数共和党人仍然表示希望看到共和党继续沿着特朗普的方向前进，

sentences.en: even though two-thirds of the country very much wants the Republican Party to do something completely different.
sentences.zh: 尽管全国有三分之二的人非常希望共和党做一些完全不同的事情。

sentences.en: So Donald Trump is still a huge limiting factor on the ability of the Republican Party to go in a new direction in the next two years.
sentences.zh: 因此，唐纳德·特朗普仍然是共和党在未来两年走向新方向的巨大制约因素。

sentences.en: Nate, what you just described, this nub of what's left of the president's support, is what I think we've long understood to be a cult of personality.
sentences.zh: 内特，你刚才描述的这些总统支持者的残余核心，就是我们长期以来所理解的个人崇拜。

sentences.en: The coalition that you all at this table have said basically disintegrated tonight was what he borrowed and put together beyond that nub.
sentences.zh: 你们在座各位刚才说在今晚基本上已经瓦解的联盟，是他借来并在这个核心之外拼凑起来的。

sentences.en: And it was based on policies and promises.
sentences.zh: 它是建立在政策和承诺的基础上的。

sentences.en: And on Tuesday night, a lot of voters of both parties felt that those promises were not kept, those policies hurt them, and they moved away from him.
sentences.zh: 而在周二晚上，两党的许多选民觉得这些承诺没有兑现，这些政策伤害了他们，于是他们离他而去。

sentences.en: But there still is at the core this group that won't move away from him that probably keeps the rest of the party from being able to move away from him too?
sentences.zh: 但在核心地带仍然有一群不会离开他的人，这可能也让党内其他人无法离开他？

sentences.en: Or no?
sentences.zh: 还是说不是这样？

sentences.en: That seems to be the central question.
sentences.zh: 这似乎是核心问题。

sentences.en: The Republican Party is in a really tough spot.
sentences.zh: 共和党处境非常艰难。

sentences.en: Donald Trump destroyed it as we knew it, and he remains the center of gravity.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普摧毁了我们所熟知的共和党，而他依然是重力中心。

sentences.en: Everyone is stuck in orbit around him, even though it now feels like a political black hole for them that they can't escape from, even though they'd love to.
sentences.zh: 每个人都被困在他的轨道上运行，尽管对他们来说，这现在感觉像是一个无法逃脱的政治黑洞，即便他们很想逃离。

sentences.en: I think that the president has clearly lost basically the entire periphery of his coalition.
sentences.zh: 我认为总统显然基本上失去了他联盟的所有外围力量。

sentences.en: All of the young and non-white voters who put him over the top in 2024, many of the white working class voters that put him over the top in 2026,
sentences.zh: 所有在2024年将他推向顶峰的年轻和非白人选民，许多在2026年将他推向顶峰的白人工人阶级选民，

sentences.en: and even some of the moderate Republicans who maybe backed Nikki Haley and long before Mitt Romney who have been consistent Republicans all along
sentences.zh: 甚至还有一些温和派共和党人，他们可能支持过妮基·黑利，更早之前支持过米特·罗姆尼，他们一直都是坚定的共和党人，

sentences.en: and reduced him just to this core of MAGA superfans and the most consistent Republicans who would never consider voting for the Democratic Party.
sentences.zh: 而这最终将他缩减为仅剩MAGA超级粉丝和那些绝对不会考虑投票给民主党的坚定共和党人这一核心。

sentences.en: And the core problem is that may still be a majority of the Republican primary electorate.
sentences.zh: 核心问题在于，这可能仍然是共和党初选选民中的大多数。

sentences.en: The ones picking the candidates who run as Republicans.
sentences.zh: 那些挑选作为共和党人参选的候选人的人。

sentences.en: Think about this year.
sentences.zh: 想想今年。

sentences.en: You could not win a Republican primary this year without President Trump, and then you could not win a general election with him.
sentences.zh: 今年如果没有特朗普总统，你根本赢不了共和党初选，但有了他，你就赢不了大选。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: That's a big old conundrum.
sentences.zh: 这真是一个老大的难题。

sentences.en: That's the trap.
sentences.zh: 这就是陷阱。

sentences.en: Friends, it is 2.10 a.m., and as a final question to all three of you, I want you to talk about your big questions this morning
sentences.zh: 朋友们，现在是凌晨两点十分，作为给你们三个人的最后一个问题，我想请你们谈谈在今天早上

sentences.en: as we enter a new political landscape, maybe even a new political era, in which the United States House of Representatives, the United States Senate
sentences.zh: 当我们进入一个新的政治格局，甚至可能是一个新的政治时代时，你们心中的重大问题是什么？在这个时代里，美国众议院、美国参议院

sentences.en: are comfortably controlled by Democrats in the final two years of President Trump's second and final term.
sentences.zh: 在特朗普总统第二任期也是最后一任期的最后两年里，由民主党舒适地把控着。

sentences.en: What are the big questions you have in your head as we look forward to the next few months and the next two years?
sentences.zh: 当我们展望未来几个月和未来两年时，你们脑海中的重大问题是什么？

sentences.en: Shane?
sentences.zh: 肖恩？

sentences.en: I mean, I want to know about J.D.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我想了解J·D·

sentences.en: Vance.
sentences.zh: 万斯。

sentences.en: Oh, that's good.
sentences.zh: 哦，这很好。

sentences.en: I think that nobody encapsulates that Trump trap more.
sentences.zh: 我认为没有人比他更能体现那个特朗普陷阱了。

sentences.en: He is the sitting vice president, the frontrunner to be the next nominee, and yet there is probably no one who can maneuver less away from Donald Trump than J.D.
sentences.zh: 他是现任副总统，是下一届总统候选人提名的领跑者，然而，可能没有人比J·D·

sentences.en: Vance.
sentences.zh: 万斯更无法摆脱唐纳德·特朗普了。

sentences.en: And how does he navigate this moment in the coming months if he campaigns, as most people presume he will?
sentences.zh: 如果他像大多数人预期的那样参加竞选，他将如何在接下来的几个月中应对这个时刻？

sentences.en: Kamala Harris taught us a valuable lesson about what happens when you are the closely aligned figure to an unpopular or declining political figure in the president you're under.
sentences.zh: 卡玛拉·哈里斯给我们上了一课，让我们明白当你与一个不受欢迎或日渐式微的政治人物、也就是你所依附的总统紧密绑定时会发生什么。

sentences.en: I think one of the big questions is what does the Democratic Party become?
sentences.zh: 我认为其中一个重大问题是民主党将变成什么样？

sentences.en: I think for a decade they have organized themselves in opposition to Trump.
sentences.zh: 我认为十年来，他们一直以反对特朗普来组织自己。

sentences.en: He's been the biggest energizer for their voters, and that's been like a central organizing principle of being a Democrat.
sentences.zh: 他是他们选民最大的赋能者，这一直是作为一名民主党人的核心组织原则。

sentences.en: And now, for all the reasons we said, Trump is going to be declining in power, declining as an organizing force in our politics,
sentences.zh: 现在，由于我们所说的种种原因，特朗普的力量将不断衰退，作为我们政治中组织力量的作用也将衰退，

sentences.en: and that leaves Democrats trying to figure out with all these wins, what does their party stand for, and what is their coalition,
sentences.zh: 这使得民主党人在取得所有这些胜利之后，不得不去弄清楚他们的党代表什么，他们的联盟是什么，

sentences.en: and who do they become in an era where Trump is no longer the dominant force?
sentences.zh: 在特朗普不再是主导力量的时代，他们将成为谁？

sentences.en: If they can answer that question in a way that enough Americans like, they have a shot at the White House, and if they cannot answer that question,
sentences.zh: 如果他们能以足够多的美国人喜欢的方式回答这个问题，他们就有机会入主白宫；如果他们无法回答这个问题，

sentences.en: it's going to be really hard to win in 2028.
sentences.zh: 要在2028年获胜将非常困难。

sentences.en: Those were two great answers, and one for Democrats and one for Republicans.
sentences.zh: 这两个回答都很好，一个针对民主党，一个针对共和党。

sentences.en: Let me offer then the backdrop that maybe they'll both play off against as they try and chart their future.
sentences.zh: 那么让我提出这样一个背景，也许他们在试图规划未来时会与之进行博弈。

sentences.en: I'm interested to learn whether any Democrat offers a fundamentally different answer to what the nation's problems are.
sentences.zh: 我很想知道是否有哪个民主党人对国家的问题给出了根本不同的答案。

sentences.en: We have an argument from Democratic Socialists that says the party basically needs to move to the left, and we have a bunch of mainstream establishment Democrats who, in some ways,
sentences.zh: 我们听到了来自民主党社会主义者的观点，认为该党基本上需要向左转，我们还有一群主流建制派民主党人，在某些方面，

sentences.en: represent a continuation of the same Democratic message that we've heard in various forms since Obama.
sentences.zh: 他们代表了自奥巴马以来我们以各种形式听到的那种民主党信息的延续。

sentences.en: And when I think back to the last time a party was really discredited after 2008, the Republicans really struggled to come up with something different.
sentences.zh: 每当我回想起2008年后一个政党真正声誉扫地的时候，共和党人确实很难想出什么不同的对策。

sentences.en: They kind of just tried to rerun being a Reagan-Romney Republican in 2012.
sentences.zh: 他们在2012年只是试图重操里根-罗姆尼式共和党人的旧业。

sentences.en: And it took Donald Trump coming up with a totally different theory of what the nation's problem was to break up this old system that had been kind of discredited.
sentences.zh: 直到唐纳德·特朗普提出了一套完全不同的关于国家问题所在的理论，才打破了这个已经声誉扫地的旧系统。

sentences.en: And I don't know whether a Democrat is going to come up with that in 2028, much as no one came up with it for the Republicans in 2012.
sentences.zh: 我不知道民主党人是否会在2028年想出这一点，就像2008年后没有人为2012年的共和党想出来一样。

sentences.en: But I think as we enter this new era of American politics, someone's going to come up with that new theory and new message and new policies
sentences.zh: 但我认为，当我们进入美国政治的新时代时，有人会提出那种新理论、新信息和新政策，

sentences.en: that will try and address whatever it is that's going to define American politics in the years ahead.
sentences.zh: 并试图解决未来几年定义美国政治的任何问题。

sentences.en: And you think it could happen in this moment?
sentences.zh: 你认为这可能会在这个时刻发生吗？

sentences.en: Things are changing.
sentences.zh: 事物正在发生变化。

sentences.en: And when things change, that's when politicians and politics have the opportunity to change in response.
sentences.zh: 当事物发生变化时，正是政治家和政治做出反应并随之改变的机会。

sentences.en: And Shane and Lisa, thank you for being here at this really, really late hour, early hour, depending on which way you see it.
sentences.zh: 肖恩和丽莎，谢谢你们在这个非常、非常晚的时间——或者说早晨，取决于你怎么看——来到这里。

sentences.en: Appreciate your time.
sentences.zh: 感谢你们抽出时间。

sentences.en: Thank you for having us.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我们。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: With Erica Green.
sentences.zh: 与埃里卡·格林一起。

sentences.en: Hello, Mr. Haceta.
sentences.zh: 你好，哈塞塔先生。

sentences.en: Good.
sentences.zh: 很好。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 嗨。

sentences.en: On Tuesday night, my colleagues, White House Correspondents Erica Green and Tyler Pager, spoke with President Trump by phone from the White House,
sentences.zh: 周二晚上，我的同事、白宫记者埃里卡·格林和泰勒·佩杰在白宫通过电话与特朗普总统进行了交谈，

sentences.en: as the president was still processing his party's sweeping losses in the midterm election.
sentences.zh: 当时总统还在消化他所在政党在期中选举中的惨败。

sentences.en: I'm just looking at these results as I'm talking about here.
sentences.zh: 我边说边看着这些结果。

sentences.en: I see that Darlene lost well.
sentences.zh: 我看到达琳输得很惨。

sentences.en: Including the defeat of the Republican Senate candidate in South Carolina, Darlene Graham.
sentences.zh: 包括南卡罗来纳州共和党参议员候选人达琳·格雷厄姆的落败。

sentences.en: That's amazing.
sentences.zh: 这太惊人了。

sentences.en: How do you think Lindsay would have done if he ran?
sentences.zh: 你觉得如果林赛参选的话会怎么样？

sentences.en: Trump conceded that higher gas prices from the war he launched against Iran had upset voters.
sentences.zh: 特朗普承认，他对伊朗发动的战争导致的油价上涨让选民感到不满。

sentences.en: They don't mind the Iran, but they probably weren't happy.
sentences.zh: 他们并不介意伊朗的事，但他们可能对结果不高兴。

sentences.en: They weren't happy with the oil price.
sentences.zh: 他们对油价很不满。

sentences.en: So, you know, it's one of those things.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，事情就是这样。

sentences.en: But he insisted that had he himself been on the ballot, Republicans would have performed far better in the election.
sentences.zh: 但他坚称，如果他自己参选，共和党人在这次选举中的表现会好得多。

sentences.en: Everybody's saying the same thing.
sentences.zh: 每个人都在这么说。

sentences.en: I wasn't on the ballot.
sentences.zh: 我当时没在选票上。

sentences.en: Two years ago, when I'm on the ballot, we won all of these states by a lot.
sentences.zh: 两年前我参选时，我们在所有这些州都以巨大优势获胜。

sentences.en: Erica pushed Trump on one of the biggest questions hanging over the midterMs.
sentences.zh: 埃里卡就期中选举悬而未决的最大问题之一向特朗普进行了逼问。

sentences.en: I just wanted to make sure you are prepared to accept the results of the election.
sentences.zh: 我只是想确认你是否准备好接受选举结果。

sentences.en: You've talked a lot about integrity.
sentences.zh: 你谈了很多关于诚信的问题。

sentences.en: Despite the president's long history of denying electoral losses, Trump said that he would accept Tuesday's results.
sentences.zh: 尽管总统长期以来一直否认选举失利，但特朗普表示他将接受周二的结果。

sentences.en: But I am absolutely willing to accept those results, Kim.
sentences.zh: 但我绝对愿意接受这些结果，金。

sentences.en: And he said he was prepared to work with the new Democratic majorities in both the House and the Senate,
sentences.zh: 并且他说他准备好与众议院和参议院的新民主党多数派合作，

sentences.en: even if they sought his testimony for congressional investigations into his administration.
sentences.zh: 即使他们要求他就其政府的国会调查提供证词。

sentences.en: We'll work with the Democrats.
sentences.zh: 我们会与民主党合作。

sentences.en: And we'll, you know, look forward to working with them.
sentences.zh: 而且你知道的，我们很期待与他们合作。

sentences.en: We'll probably work something out.
sentences.zh: 我们大概能达成某种协议。

sentences.en: Thank you, Mr. President, for your time.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，总统先生，感谢你接受采访。

sentences.en: Okay, thank you, Mr. President.
sentences.zh: 好的，谢谢你，总统先生。

sentences.en: Have a good time.
sentences.zh: 祝你过得愉快。

sentences.en: Bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 拜拜。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他内容。

sentences.en: In a potentially major change to U.S.
sentences.zh: 在对美国外交政策可能产生的重大改变中，

sentences.en: foreign policy, President Trump said that the bulk of American aid to Israel, about $4 billion, would be cut off at the end of this year.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统表示，美国对以色列的大部分援助（约40亿美元）将在今年年底被切断。

sentences.en: In an Election Day interview with Fox News, Trump described his motivation for the change as taking away a powerful talking point from the left wing of the Democratic Party,
sentences.zh: 在选举日接受福克斯新闻采访时，特朗普将这一改变的动机描述为剥夺民主党左翼的一个有力论据，

sentences.en: including Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan.
sentences.zh: 其中包括来自密歇根州的候任参议员阿卜杜勒·埃尔赛义德。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Because they don't need it, Brian.
sentences.zh: 因为他们不需要，布赖恩。

sentences.en: I mean, I asked them, because they don't need it, and because why should we suffer the slings from lunatics like an El-Sayed when they don't need it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我问过他们，因为他们不需要，而且为什么我们要承受像埃尔赛义德这样疯子的抨击，而他们根本不需要这些？

sentences.en: It's a bad talking point.
sentences.zh: 这是一个糟糕的论点。

sentences.en: In the aftermath of the October 7th attacks and Israel's response in Gaza, both Democratic lawmakers and candidates have become increasingly critical of U.S.
sentences.zh: 在10月7日袭击事件以及以色列在加沙的反应之后，民主党议员和候选人都越来越批评美国对以色列的军事援助。

sentences.en: military aid to Israel.
sentences.zh: 对以色列的军事援助。

sentences.en: Trump said that the decision to cut off the aid was made with the consent of Israel's leadership, but the announcement appeared to catch some Israeli officials by surprise.
sentences.zh: 特朗普表示，切断援助的决定是在征得以色列领导层同意的情况下作出的，但这一宣布似乎让一些以色列官员感到意外。

sentences.zh: 他们是全黑睡眠者吗？

sentences.zh: 我是指，他们需要什么样的光线条件？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的要求。

sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
